definitions.missingResourceTimingsLearnMoreLabel: Learn how to get visibility into cross-origin resources
definitions.missingResourceTimingsExplanation: Resource timing data collection is subject to same-origin policy restrictions. This means that collection of resource timings is restricted to resources retrieved from the origin of the HTML document and resources served by origins which explicitly allow this.
definitions.scriptErrorLearnMoreLabel: Learn how to get visibility into these errors
definitions.scriptErrorExplanation: Error type, message and stack trace are inaccessible due to browser security mechanisms, i.e. the same-origin policy. This typically means that the error was caused by a script that is hosted on an origin different from the origin of the HTML document. JavaScript files retrieved from content-delivery networks and advertisement services are most commonly responsible for these.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation02CouldNotDownloadJ: Could not download JavaScript source file because of missing authentication (HTTP status code 401).
definitions.stackTraceExplanation03CouldNotDownloadJ: Could not download JavaScript source file because of failed authorization (HTTP status code 403).
definitions.stackTraceExplanation04CouldNotDownloadJ: Could not download JavaScript source file because the file was not found (HTTP status code 404).
definitions.stackTraceExplanation05CouldNotDownloadJ: Could not download JavaScript source file because the HTTP request failed and was not a 401, 403 or 404.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation06NoReferenceToSour: No reference to source map in HTTP header nor as annotation in JavaScript source file.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation07AnUnknownErrorHap: An unknown error happened during the identification of the source map file.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation08CouldNotDownloadS: Could not download source map file because of missing authentication (HTTP response code 401).
definitions.stackTraceExplanation14CouldNotDownloadS: Could not download source map file because of failed authorization (HTTP status code 403).
definitions.stackTraceExplanation09CouldNotDownloadS: Could not download source map file because the file was not found (HTTP status code 404).
definitions.stackTraceExplanation10CouldNotDownloadS: Could not download source map file because the HTTP request failed and was not a 401, 403 or 404.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation12AnUnknownErrorOcc: An unknown error occurred while processing the source map file.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation13CouldNotFindOrigi: Could not find original mapping for a combination of line and column number via the source map. This can happen after releases for users that are running outdated versions of your JavaScript files.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation15TranslationIsOnly: Translation is only possible when a reference to a line number is included in the stack trace line.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation16ThisStackTraceLin: This stack trace line's file reference does not point to a JavaScript file. Source map based stack trace line translation only works when the source is a JavaScript file.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation17CouldCotEstablish: Could not establish a TCP / TLS connection to the host serving the JavaScript file.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation18CouldCotEstablish: Could not establish a TCP / TLS connection to the host serving the source map file.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation19ARequestTimeoutOc: A request timeout occurred when trying to retrieve the JavaScript file.
definitions.stackTraceExplanation20ARequestTimeoutOc: A request timeout occurred when trying to retrieve the JavaScript file. source map file.

trackingSnippet.enableSessionTrackingHelpText: Session tracking can be used to gain insights into the activity of end-users across page loads. By enabling session tracking, Instana can determine end-user impact in the absence of defined user information.
trackingSnippet.enableSubResourceIntegrityHelpText: Subresource Integrity (SRI) is a security feature that ensures browsers can verify the resources they fetch.
trackingSnippet.trackingSnippetPresenterEnablingModalBod: Enabling SRI is recommended for security. Ensure that you have selected the latest agent version from the dropdown.
trackingSnippet.trackingSnippetPresenterDisablingModalTi: Are you sure you want to disable Subresource Integrity (SRI)?
trackingSnippet.trackingSnippetPresenterDisablingModalFi: Disabling SRI might cause security issues.
trackingSnippet.trackingSnippetPresenterDisablingModalBo: If you decide to disable it, ensure that you are in a secure network environment. When SRI is disabled, the tracking script defaults to the latest JavaScript agent version but will not be able to ensure that browsers can verify the resources they fetch.

ipMasking.title: IP masking
ipMasking.help: IP masking protects end-user privacy by masking (anonymizing) segments of IP addresses. This happens at the earliest possible point within Instana’s ingestion pipeline so that full IP addresses are never stored. Instana always masks IP addresses using rules commonly used in the industry. You can configure stricter IP masking rules if your organization requires this.
ipMasking.option_DEFAULT: Default, mask the last 8 bits for IPv4 and the last 80 bits for IPv6
ipMasking.option_STRICT: Strict, mask the last 16 bits for IPv4 and the last 96 bits for IPv6
ipMasking.option_REMOVE_ALL_DETAILS: Remove IP addresses (only a hint of IPv4 and IPv6 usage remains)

geoDetailRemoval.title: Geographic detail removal
geoDetailRemoval.help: Instana determines an approximate geographic location for incoming data based on end-user IP addresses. This includes information about end-user coordinates, city, state, country and continent information. Some organizations may consider this data to be end-user identifiable and may therefore desire to further anonymize this approximate location information. This can be achieved using our geographic detail removal.
geoDetailRemoval.option_REMOVE_COORDINATES: Remove latitude, longitude and accuracy information
geoDetailRemoval.option_REMOVE_CITY: Remove city, latitude, longitude and accuracy information

customGeoDetails.title: Custom geographic details
customGeoDetails.help1: Instana maps end-user IP addresses to geographic details, e.g., city and country names. This is done by inspecting various HTTP headers to retrieve the end-user IP addresses. These IP addresses are then translated to geographic details with the help of <maxmind>Maxmind's geographic databases</maxmind>. The main use case for these custom mapping rules are private networks. For example, when accessing (self-hosted) Instana installations through private networks. In such cases, public geographic databases will never contain relevant information and as such the translation process will provide either no results or only wrong/unhelpful results.
customGeoDetails.help2: Rules for custom geographic details are always expressed through comma-separated values (CSV). The CSV format and usage of our Web REST API is defined within our <documentation>documentation</documentation>.

uploader.title: Upload new rules
uploader.help: Custom geographic detail rules are defined CSV files and uploaded through our Web REST API or through this form. For more information on the file structure, limits and Web REST API please refer to our <documentation>documentation</documentation>.
uploader.failureToCallApiForStatusCodeReason: HTTP call returned with erroneous result: {{error}}

configuration.fileDownloadConfigurationDialogPathValid: At least one matching rule is required.
configuration.fileDownloadConfigurationDialogAtMostOne: The segment match condition can only contain at most one wildcard character.
configuration.fileDownloadConfigurationDialogPathValid: Path matching rules must start with a slash character: /
configuration.fileDownloadConfigurationDialogMatchingR: You can define multiple matching rules to describe when we should include your configuration in HTTP requests.  We make use of your configured HTTP basic authentication and custom HTTP headers when at least one matching rule matches the file's URL.
We recommend only to match files for the {{http}} scheme as your configuration will otherwise be transmitted in plain text!
configuration.fileDownloadConfigurationDialogLabelHost: Describe how to match the host segment of URLs. You can define wildcard matching via {{asterisks}}
configuration.fileDownloadConfigurationDialogLabelPath: Describe how to match the path segment of URLs. You can define wildcard matching via {{asterisks}}
configuration.fileDownloadConfigurationDialogHTTPBasic: We recommend authentication via <linkToDocs>HTTP basic authentication</linkToDocs>. HTTP basic authentication can be easily added to most HTTP servers and proxies, e.g. Apache Httpd and Nginx.
configuration.fileDownloadConfigurationDialogCustomHTT: Custom HTTP headers are useful to support authentication mechanisms other than HTTP basic authentication or to circumvent security mechanisms commonly available in content-delivery networks, e.g. bot detection.
configuration.fileUploadConfigurationDialogDescription: An upload configuration will help you to better organize your uploaded files.
configuration.fileUploadConfigurationDialogOpenAPIHelp: Upload your files by calling Instana's Web REST API. This could be integrated into your pipeline process for automated deployment. The explaination and usage of our Web REST API is defined within our <documentation>documentation</documentation>.
configuration.stackTraceTranslationExplanationWithUplo: To make JavaScript stack traces more readable, e.g. to show references to non minified files and lines, Instana needs to access JavaScript and source map files. Adding a download configuration here allows Instana's server to authenticate and download these files in order to provide more insights into JavaScript errors. If your files are hosted privately and cannot be accessed by Instana, then an upload configuration could be used in this scenario by uploading your files manually through our Web REST API.
